caps_triggered.evidence: The required public preview and the in-repo evidence are not the submitted build. README.md:5 advertises https://patanakiat.github.io/data-detective/ ; that URL serves the round-0 files — the live index.html still contains 'The population value is about 22%' (true value 25.2%) and the live data.js still contains the Math.max(0,…) clamp that floors 16 weeks. git status shows every round-1 edit uncommitted (M app.js, data.js, model.js, index.html, styles.css, …) and origin/main is still 076beef 'build: round 0'. TEST_REPORT.md:34-38 quotes the new values (1.8 %, 0.81, 56.4 %) but the screenshots it tells the judge to open (docs/screenshots/shot-a1-framing-desktop.png shows '4.7 px' with the title/tick collision; docs/screenshots/shot-a3-correlation-tablet.png shows 0.82 and the origin pile) are the superseded build. Definition of done #5 ('the GitHub Pages preview matches the submitted archive') fails and the acceptance-example → screenshot mapping is hollow.

verdict: The authored build is strong: all three carry-over items are genuinely fixed in the source and visible in the round-2 captures, the 16 tests run and pass with the documented command, and the charts are legible and numerically honest at 360/768/1280. But the submission is not what is shipped — the README's live preview serves the round-0 build (still 'about 22%', still clamped weeks) and the repo's own evidence screenshots show '4.7 px' and 0.82, because every round-1 fix is uncommitted and origin/main is still the round-0 commit. Definition of done #5 fails and the acceptance-example evidence mapping is hollow, so the missing-deliverable cap holds the score at 5.

gap_to_10: Seeing Theory (Brown University) — the interaction is the explanation: you manipulate a live simulation (watch a sampling distribution build as n grows, move a parameter and see the consequence) and the idea lands in the hand. This lesson's statistics are real and its framing stat is viewport-true, but Activity 2 is a dot plot you append to one draw at a time — there is no repeated-sampling animation, no accumulating sampling-distribution view, and the exercises around the charts are checkbox questions, so the misconception is corrected by copy rather than by felt experience. And no gap to 10 closes until the deployed build equals the archive.
